meta_description: The Peter and the Wolf story and moral, Prokofiev's musical original, and read-aloud tips that teach children courage and wisdom. A guide to this musical classic for ages 4–7.

content.alt: Peter and the Wolf - What kind of story is Peter and the Wolf?
content.text:
What kind of story is Peter and the Wolf?

Peter and the Wolf is the tale of a brave boy named Peter who, together with his animal friends, uses his wits to catch a wolf. It's famous as a musical story in which each character is represented by a different instrument. Enjoy the story and the music together while learning about courage.
content.caption: A story you meet through music

content.alt: Peter and the Wolf - The original Peter and the Wolf story
content.text:
The original Peter and the Wolf story

It is a musical tale composed in 1936 by the Russian composer Sergei Prokofiev. By representing the characters with instruments — Peter as the strings, the bird as the flute, the duck as the oboe, the cat as the clarinet, and the wolf as the horns — it's a classic crafted to let children learn the instruments of the orchestra naturally.
content.caption: A different voice for every instrument

content.alt: Peter and the Wolf - A summary of the Peter and the Wolf story
content.text:
A summary of the Peter and the Wolf story

Despite his grandfather's warning, Peter heads out into the meadow with his friend the bird. When a wolf appears and swallows the duck, Peter, unafraid, works together with the bird to catch the wolf with a rope. It's a brave ending in which he and the hunters capture the wolf and take it to the zoo.
content.caption: A victory of courage and teamwork

content.alt: Peter and the Wolf - The moral of Peter and the Wolf
content.text:
The moral of Peter and the Wolf

The heart of it is that even in a frightening situation you can face it with courage and wisdom, and by working together with friends you can accomplish even great things. Talk with your child about, "How do you find courage when you're scared?"
content.caption: A victory that courage brought about

content.alt: Peter and the Wolf - How to read it aloud to your child
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Play Prokofiev's music in the background, and when an instrument's sound comes in, ask, "Whose sound is this?" and guess the character together. Change your voice for each character, and read the wolf-catching scene with real excitement! Best suited for ages 4–7.
content.caption: A story you both hear and see

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is Peter and the Wolf good for?
A. It's best suited for ages 4–7. Listening along with the music, children naturally pick up the instruments and the orchestra too.

Q. Why is it a musical fairy tale?
A. Because it's a work crafted so that each character is expressed by a different instrument, letting children learn the sounds of the instruments as they listen to the story.

Q. What activities go well with it?
A. Guessing the instrument sounds, imitating the characters' voices, and listening to orchestra music all work well.
